observation_summary: The MutableDateTime object's value was incorrectly modified when adding zero units (e.g., addDays(0)) during a DST transition, causing an unexpected shift in the time zone offset.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a conditional check (if amount != 0) to prevent unnecessary and incorrect recalculations of the internal millisecond value when the addition amount is zero. This is a classic case of missing validation/checking for a trivial input case that leads to side effects in complex logic.
evidence_used: The bug report states that addDays(0) changes the value of the object during DST transitions.
The fix diff shows that for every 'add' method (addYears, addMonths, addDays, etc.), a check 'if (amount != 0)' was added to wrap the existing 'setMillis' call.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix changes the execution flow, it does not reimplement the underlying date-time arithmetic algorithm; it simply adds a guard clause to skip the algorithm when it is unnecessary.
